title: Leaving New Orleans with Mabel Elaine's jazz band show
summary: Garland describes leaving for Chicago with a stage show, Mabel Elaine and her jazz band, bringing his own New Orleans players; the drummer Happy was nearly left behind.

bands.name: Mabel Elaine and her jazz band

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How did you happen to leave New Orleans? What happened? Well, Freddie Keppert was playing for a girl by the name they called Mabel Elaine.

No. Mabel Elaine and her jazz band. She's a white girl. She used to clunk band. You know how Boa Jingles used to dance with wooden shoes on. She had the same thing. She used to be in a bale of cotton. She was blackface. When you get on the stage, that bale of cotton was out there. They couldn't go out. We'd be all lying around in this cotton, see, with a couple of holes on, satin cover holes, different colors, and bandana, hangers, and hats. So I had, when we started playing, this fave of cotton opened up. And she'd come out there. It was a pretty good show. Was this on the stage? On the stage. We were on off in time. Yeah. Mabel Elaine and her jazz band. And this big boat was the Robert E. Lee. This was in Chicago? That's why I thought it was Mabel Elaine. No. Well, that's how I come to go to Chicago. Freddie's telling you, Freddie Keppert was playing for him. Freddie and them got to New York. He got a job in New York or something, and he quit. And this man sent for another band. Then Manuel Perez come out with a bunch. But then they said, I come right behind Manuel Perez and them, and went with this girl, Mabel Elaine. And then they said, I'm a little bit. I brought Sugar Johnny, trumpet, Louis Keppert on guitar, Roy Palmer on trombone, Herbert Lindsay on violin, and a boy named Lawrence Duell on clarinet, myself on bass. And I had Happy to play drum, and just as we were fixed, Happy was fixed to get on the train, here comes the telegram. And the agent down there, you know, the man who was looking out for us, setting us off, he said, Stop Happy called me, he came in and told him, I said, Don't bring the drummer. Poor little Happy like to die. Just fixed to get up on the train with his drums, you know, at the Union Station in New Orleans. I would have New Orleans.
Yeah, he fixed to get on this thing.
Was it your band where you lead drove the band?
Me, I was the head of the band. So we went on, and we left Mabel Elaine, out there. The show closed, that's what it was. Now they go on their vacation.
Well, did you go on the train to Chicago?
Right to Chicago, on the other one, to Illinois. Illinois, I said.
